messages.content:
You are an experimental Clojure RLM. Investigate observations through context handles
and SCI. Keep large records outside your prompt: select and compute with code, and read
only what you need. You may delegate a subtask with selected evidence to a child session.

Act only through the provided tools. Every response must make exactly one tool call.
Text outside a tool call is never executed. Finish by calling done. For a long result,
build it in SCI and pass done a source expression instead of typing the result.

repl_eval runs Clojure in SCI:
- Send one or more forms; they run in order and the last value is the result.
- A def shows its var name, so definitions need no trailing nil. The value of every result is also bound to last-result.
- Helpers: (parse-long s) returns an integer or nil; context-lines is the context as a vector of lines; (page v offset n) returns n characters of v's printed text from offset; subs is bounded to the string, so (subs s 0 3000) never fails on a shorter s.
- A result larger than about 60 KB comes back as a preview with a truncation note, and the worker keeps running. Its full value is bound to full-result, which paging does not change; read the rest with (page full-result offset n).
- Clojure reader syntax works: #"\d+" (no double escaping), #(...), 'x, @x and #'v. #= and tagged literals such as #inst are refused.
- clojure.string and String methods such as (.indexOf s "x") work, as does Integer/parseInt; Long, Math and Character classes do not.
- read-string, eval, slurp, spit and printing (println, pr-str) are denied; build text with str and clojure.string.
Errors come back as tool results with a hint; fix the code and call again.

The controller rejects a response that does not make exactly one valid tool call. It
never executes text or a rejected call. For a bounded formatting failure it may request
one new response. That correction uses the shared call, token, cost and time budgets,
and only one is allowed across the whole task, including child sessions.

This is an external-context benchmark. The immutable complete public text is already bound to external-context in each SCI worker. Inspect or compute over it through repl_eval without loading it into the model window. The context handle also permits line queries. Finish with done: put the exact benchmark answer in summary, or compute it in SCI and pass source. The answer is scored externally.

{:task {:question "The context window contains thousands of general-knowledge questions, one per line. Each line has a User ID, which is not necessarily unique (each User ID can be associated with multiple questions). Each question has an answer that can be described as one of 6 categories: 'numeric value', 'entity', 'location', 'description and abstract concept', 'abbreviation', 'human being' — they are not explicitly labeled, so you must infer the label from the semantics of each question.

You will be asked to compute exact aggregate label statistics over pairs of users. Do not guess, estimate, or approximate the result — calculate the exact answer.

In the above data, list all pairs of user IDs (no duplicate pairs, list lower ID first) where both users have at least one instance with a description and abstract concept or numeric value, and all instances that are a numeric value for both users must be after February 1, 2023. Each of the questions can be labelled as one of the labels (the data does not provide the labels, you need to figure out the label from the semantics of the question): description and abstract concept, entity, human being, numeric value, location, abbreviation. In your answer, list all pairs in the format (user_id_1, user_id_2), separated by newlines.

Return every matching pair as (user_id_1, user_id_2), one per line, sorted by the first user ID. If there are no matching pairs, return exactly [].", :task_id "oolong-pairs-validation-32768-7"}, :context-handle "context", :repl-binding "external-context"}

content.thinking:
I've got 787 questions to label, which is too many to do by hand, so I'll write a keyword heuristic in code to tag each one as numeric or description. The condition is that both users need at least one desc or numeric instance, and every numeric instance for both users has to fall after February 1, 2023.

I'm now settling on the keyword lists for the numeric and description labels, and then I'll run the check that both users have at least one tagged item and that every numeric item falls after February 1, 2023.

input.source:
(def rows (keep #(when-let [m (re-matches #"Date: (\w+) (\d+), (\d+) \|\| User: (\d+) \|\| Instance: (.*)" %)] m) context-lines))
(def mon {"Jan" 1 "Feb" 2})
(defn after? [[_ m d y]] (let [y (parse-long y) mo (get mon m 3) d (parse-long d)] (or (> y 2023) (and (= y 2023) (or (> mo 2) (and (= mo 2) (> d 1)))))))
(defn lab [q] (let [s (.toLowerCase q)]
 (cond (re-find #"stand for|abbreviat|acronym" s) :abb
  (re-find #"how (many|much|long|far|old|big|tall|high|fast|large|hot|cold|deep|wide)|what year|when |what date|population|how often|what (is|was) the (number|average|speed|height|weight|temperature|cost|price|age|distance)|percent|what time|which year|how heavy" s) :num
  (re-find #"^who |who (is|was|were)|what (person|man|woman)" s) :hum
  (re-find #"^where |what (country|city|state|continent)|which (country|city|state)" s) :loc
  (re-find #"^why |^how |what (is|are|was) (a|an|the)? ?[a-z ]*\?|^what does .* mean|definition|meaning" s) :desc
  :else :ent)))
(def L (map (fn [r] {:u (nth r 4) :d (after? r) :l (lab (nth r 5))}) rows))
(def info (into {} (for [[u rs] (group-by :u L)] [u {:ok (boolean (some #(#{:desc :num} (:l %)) rs)) :n (every? :d (filter #(= :num (:l %)) rs))}])))
(def good (sort (map key (filter (fn [[_ v]] (and (:ok v) (:n v))) info))))
(count rows) (count good)
(clojure.string/join "\n" (for [a good b good :when (< (parse-long a) (parse-long b))] (str "(" a ", " b ")")))
